joint_initial_state_note: Combined-input cases start from a phase-zero affine combination of the qualified endpoint nodal fields. This is an initialization guess only; all reported joint results come from full nonlinear ANSYS runs with independently checked final periodicity. Chosen before observing joint-case results.
purpose: Assumption-based input uncertainty screening of the reconstructed model; not experimental validation or a statistical explanation of the source-paper discrepancy.
range_basis: The paper supplies nominal constants, not uncertainty intervals. All half-widths below are analyst-declared engineering assumptions, fixed before the scenario results.
distribution_assumption: Independent uniform normalized inputs on [-1,1]; capacity_scale is one correlated multiplier on all material heat capacities. No measured probabilities are claimed.

external_epsilon.scope: exterior thermal emission and Earth-IR absorption together

capacity_scale.scope: all specific heat capacities; density and geometry fixed

method: Paired full-ANSYS endpoint scenarios, local central-difference response propagation and midpoint-curvature checks. Numerical resolution effects are reported separately and are not disguised as physical input uncertainty.
exclusions: orbital beta, attitude and ephemeris uncertainty
model-form disagreement with the source solver
joint_check_design: After paired screening, choose the high/low endpoint of each factor that raises battery average at the nominal battery-peak phase. Solve that combined corner and its opposite with full nonlinear ANSYS. These check the affine approximation; they are not reference-data fits.
curvature_interpretation: Midpoint deviations are compared with the magnitude of input responses. Orbital periodicity defects and numerical-resolution changes limit interpretation of small curvature values.
periodicity_tightening_basis: Tightened from 0.1 K after observing the capacity_scale=0.9 cycle defect of 0.0756 K. Smaller sensitivities and curvature checks require lower residual drift. This changes numerical qualification only; all physical ranges and nominal values remain fixed.
